author: Adam Ripple
title: Shane Smith takes over North Star football team with loaded roster - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Ripple ,
19 hours ago North Star principal Louis Lepley says players and parents wanted change within the football program, comparing it to that of the Pittsburgh Steelers and Mike Tomlin, wanting to see growth and advancement in the program.
That change occurred as Bob Landis was not brought back as head coach after six seasons with the program.
The North Star Board of Directors hired Landis' former assistant Shane Smith as the new head coach in the offseason. Smith was on Landis' staff for three seasons. Not many coaches take over a team with true district title aspirations and potential. However, that is exactly what Smith walked himself into.
"Bob (Landis) had everything set in place here," said Smith. "There's a lot of experience led by the seniors. We have 16 seniors, and that makes my job a heck of a lot easier as a coach. We are going to take it a week at a time and see what happens. The main thing is staying healthy."
Job opening North Star Board opens head football coaching position
Fresh face Former North Star assistant hired as new head football coach
The Cougars will go behind a veteran offensive line, including Brady Meyers, Johnathan Kennell, Heath Landis, Brody Shroyer, transfer Mason Horner and 4-year starting quarterback Kasey Yoder.
"Our strength is those big offensive linemen," Smith said. "We think we are going to be able to run the football, and we are going to see if anyone can stop it."
Yoder had a sub-par season for his standards, completing 66 of 138 passes for 972 yards, six touchdowns and 11 interceptions. His dual-threat ability makes him dangerous. He rushed for 806 yards and 10 scores a season ago.
Running back Will Eshleman, athlete Ace Kolson, who transferred to North Star in the spring, and tight end John-Michael Steltzer will help Yoder spread the wealth on offense.
The Cougars dropped four games by eight points or less a season ago. North Star is thin on the backside of the defense after losing all-state defensive back Bryson Durst to graduation. Meyers, Yoder and Landis are the top returning tacklers from a season ago. Smith and company need contributions from some fresh faces.
"We need some young guys to step up," Smith said. "We have speed on defense. We just have to make sure we are in the right place at all times."
Coach: Shane Smith – First season, 0-0 career record
2025 record: 3-6 in Inter-County Conference, 4-6 overall
Top players lost: Bryson Durst (WR/DB), Cash Hawkins (WR/DB), Ian Koval (RB/DL), Luke Barron (OL/DL).
Top returning players: Kasey Yoder (QB/DB), Brady Meyers (OL/DL), Johnathan Kennell (OL/DL), John-Michael Steltzer (TE/DL), Brody Shroyer (OL/DL).
Assistant coaches: Zach Baker, Jeremy Nicholson, Christian Boyd, Ethan Smith, Mitchel Pristas, Rob Kolson.
District/classification: 5-2A
Last district playoff appearance: 2024
Last district playoff win: 2012
District titles in program history: Three
